q: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars designed to measure architectures against best practices. Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars?
options: A) Performance Efficiency[cite: 10]
B) Sustainability[cite: 10]
C) Operational Excellence[cite: 10]
D) Agility and Elasticity[cite: 10]
exp: The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. Agility and Elasticity is not a distinct pillar[cite: 10].

q: An organization relies heavily on Amazon S3 to store rapidly mutating transactional SQL records, causing severe performance degradation. Which Performance Design Principle is explicitly being violated in this scenario?
options: A) Consider mechanical sympathy[cite: 10]
B) Democratize advanced technologies[cite: 10]
C) Use serverless architectures[cite: 10]
D) Experiment more often[cite: 10]
exp: Mechanical sympathy means using a technology for what it was designed for. Using S3 (an object store) as a relational database violates this principle[cite: 10].

q: According to the 'Democratize advanced technologies' design principle, which TWO of the following actions align with the AWS recommendation to delegate complex tasks to the cloud vendor? (Select 2)
options: A) Consuming machine learning as a managed service rather than requiring the IT team to learn how to host and run the underlying technology[cite: 10]
B) Utilizing a managed NoSQL database service instead of manually provisioning and configuring database clusters[cite: 10]
C) Building custom data center cooling units using open-source hardware designs
D) Manually compiling media transcoding binaries on raw EC2 instances
exp: Democratizing advanced technologies means consuming complex technologies (like NoSQL, media transcoding, and machine learning) as a service rather than building and managing them internally[cite: 10].

q: Which of the following best describes the implementation of the 'Experiment more often' design principle for performance?
options: A) Creating short-lived pre-production environments to try new scenarios and architectures as new ideas emerge, utilizing virtual and automatable resources[cite: 10]
B) Running beta software directly in the primary production VPC without metrics
C) Deploying workloads to all global regions simultaneously before performing local tests
D) Replacing all serverless services with physical hardware servers for experimentation
exp: The 'Experiment more often' principle encourages using virtual, automatable resources to create short-lived pre-production environments to try new scenarios and patterns[cite: 10].

q: An architect replaces a fleet of EC2 web servers with an Amazon S3 static website and an event-driven architecture. Which performance design principle does this most directly satisfy?
options: A) Use serverless architectures[cite: 10]
B) Go global in minutes[cite: 10]
C) Democratize advanced technologies[cite: 10]
D) Consider mechanical sympathy[cite: 10]
exp: Using serverless storage services (like S3) for static websites removes the need to run and maintain physical servers, fulfilling the 'Use serverless architectures' principle[cite: 10].

q: A team requires the absolute fastest access to their S3 files and decides to evaluate the new S3 Express Zone for performance. Which Performance Design Principle does testing this new feature align with?
options: A) Experiment More Often[cite: 10]
B) Democratize advanced technologies[cite: 10]
C) Consider mechanical sympathy[cite: 10]
D) Go global in minutes[cite: 10]
exp: Testing out a new feature like the S3 Express Zone to evaluate if it provides faster access represents the 'Experiment More Often' design principle[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO of the following are explicitly listed as major categories that all performance actions will affect within AWS? (Select 2)
options: A) Compute and Hardware[cite: 10]
B) Process and Culture[cite: 10]
C) Financial Budget Allocation
D) Human Resources Recruitment
exp: The major categories for performance in AWS are Overall Architecture Selection, Compute and Hardware, Data Management, Networking and Content Delivery, and Process and Culture[cite: 10].

q: According to the Architecture Selection best practices (PERF01), which action is critical when deciding on an architectural approach to ensure business viability?
options: A) Factor cost into architectural decisions[cite: 10]
B) Ensure every service used is strictly Serverless
C) Only use third-party SaaS vendors
D) Ignore trade-offs to prioritize raw compute speed
exp: PERF01-BP03 explicitly states to 'Factor cost into architectural decisions' to find an approach that matches needs with the minimal amount of investment[cite: 10].

q: A workload requires specialized mathematical processing that standard CPUs cannot handle efficiently. According to the Compute Performance best practices (PERF02), what should the architect do?
options: A) Use optimized hardware-based compute accelerators[cite: 10]
B) Scale compute resources manually instead of dynamically
C) Use standard EC2 instances and write custom assembly code
D) Decrease the size of the compute resource to save money
exp: PERF02-BP06 specifically recommends to 'Use optimized hardware-based compute accelerators' to optimize performance efficiency for specialized workloads[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO of the following are considered Data Management Performance best practices (PERF03) according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Select 2)
options: A) Use a purpose-built data store that best supports your data access and storage requirements[cite: 10]
B) Implement data access patterns that utilize caching[cite: 10]
C) Always utilize block storage instead of object storage to ensure sequential read performance
D) Limit all database writes to a single Availability Zone to prevent jitter
exp: PERF03-BP01 (Use a purpose-built data store) and PERF03-BP05 (Implement data access patterns that utilize caching) are documented best practices for Data Management Performance[cite: 10].

q: An architect is tasked with reducing network distance and jitter for a globally distributed workload. Which TWO AWS networking features are specifically highlighted in the framework to address this?
options: A) Amazon Route 53 latency routing[cite: 10]
B) AWS Global Accelerator[cite: 10]
C) Amazon EC2 networking optimized instances
D) Amazon S3 transfer acceleration
exp: The handbook explicitly differentiates between features that optimize network traffic (EC2 optimized instances, S3 transfer acceleration, CloudFront) and features that reduce network distance or jitter (Route 53 latency routing, VPC endpoints, Direct Connect, and Global Accelerator)[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO of the following AWS product features are specifically categorized as optimizing network traffic (throughput/performance) rather than reducing network distance/jitter? (Select 2)
options: A) Enhanced Networking[cite: 10]
B) Amazon S3 transfer acceleration[cite: 10]
C) Amazon VPC endpoints
D) AWS Direct Connect
exp: Enhanced Networking, EC2 networking optimized instances, S3 transfer acceleration, and CloudFront are categorized under optimizing network traffic. VPC endpoints and Direct Connect are categorized under reducing network distance/jitter[cite: 10].

q: When generating load to test application performance, what characteristic should the test scripts possess to yield valid results?
options: A) They should be idempotent and not coupled, replicating the behavior of usage in production[cite: 10]
B) They should only run against the database layer, bypassing the application layer
C) They should be heavily coupled to ensure sequential transaction tracking
D) They must execute strictly on on-premises hardware
exp: The framework states that test scripts for load generation should replicate synthetic or prerecorded user journeys, and 'These scripts should be idempotent and not coupled' to yield valid results[cite: 10].

q: According to the Process and Culture guidelines, why is it critical to focus on the 99.9th and 99.99th percentile for latency outliers rather than just average latency?
options: A) Because if even one request out of 10,000 causes extreme latency, it creates a poor customer experience that will become a significant problem as traffic grows[cite: 10]
B) Because average latency metrics cannot be visualized in CloudWatch Dashboards
C) Because the 99.9th percentile consumes fewer monitoring resources to calculate
D) Because outliers indicate active DDoS attacks at the transport layer
exp: AWS emphasizes focusing on latency outliers because 'if one in 100 of your requests causes extreme latency, it will eventually become a problem as your traffic grows', making the average latency an insufficient metric for customer experience[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO of the following are defined as Process and Culture best practices (PERF05) for performance efficiency? (Select 2)
options: A) Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure workload health and performance[cite: 10]
B) Use automation to proactively remediate performance-related issues[cite: 10]
C) Rely strictly on manual execution for all performance test benchmarks
D) Implement static hardware limits to contain infrastructure costs
exp: PERF05-BP01 (Establish KPIs) and PERF05-BP05 (Use automation to proactively remediate performance-related issues) are explicit best practices for Process and Culture[cite: 10].

q: According to the AWS autoscaling support matrix, which service supports CLI, SDK, and CloudFormation access for autoscaling, but does NOT support Console access?
options: A) Lambda[cite: 10]
B) Amazon Comprehend
C) Amazon Neptune
D) Spot Fleet
exp: The 'Autoscaling vs Manual Scaling' table explicitly lists Lambda as having 'No' for Console access regarding autoscaling, while having 'Yes' for CLI, SDK, and CloudFormation[cite: 10].

q: According to the provided AWS service autoscaling matrix, which access method is explicitly marked as 'No' (unsupported) for Amazon Neptune?
options: A) SDK access[cite: 10]
B) Console access
C) CLI access
D) CloudFormation access
exp: In the autoscaling table, Amazon Neptune is listed with 'Yes' for Console, 'Yes' for CLI, 'Yes' for CloudFormation, but 'No' for SDK access[cite: 10].

q: Based on the autoscaling support matrix, which access method is NOT supported for configuring autoscaling on Amazon Comprehend?
options: A) Console access[cite: 10]
B) CLI access
C) SDK access
D) CloudFormation access
exp: The autoscaling table lists Amazon Comprehend as having 'No' for Console access, but 'Yes' for CLI, SDK, and CloudFormation[cite: 10].

q: When looking at 'Custom resources' in the autoscaling matrix, which configuration mechanism is NOT supported?
options: A) Console access[cite: 10]
B) CLI access
C) SDK access
D) CloudFormation access
exp: Custom resources support CLI, SDK, and CloudFormation ('Yes'), but lack Console access ('No') for autoscaling configuration[cite: 10].

q: To distribute load and increase performance on an Amazon RDS architecture, an architect adds read replicas. How is data transmitted from the primary database to the read replicas?
options: A) Asynchronous replication[cite: 10]
B) Synchronous replication
C) Global Table synchronization
D) Scheduled batch jobs
exp: The 'Offloading and Load Distribution' architectural diagram for RDS explicitly labels the connection between the primary database and the read replica as 'Asynchronous replication'[cite: 10].

q: In an Amazon Aurora DB Cluster designed for read offloading, which TWO statements accurately describe the relationship between instances and storage? (Select 2)
options: A) Both the Primary Instance and the Aurora Replicas share the same underlying Cluster Volume[cite: 10]
B) The Primary Instance executes both Reads and Writes to the Cluster Volume[cite: 10]
C) Aurora Replicas perform asynchronous writes back to the Primary Instance
D) The Cluster Volume is completely isolated per Availability Zone without sharing
exp: The Aurora diagram shows the Primary Instance processing 'Reads' and 'Writes' to a shared 'Cluster Volume' spanning multiple AZs, which is also read by the Aurora Replicas[cite: 10].

q: When setting up read replicas in Amazon ElastiCache across multiple regions to distribute load, how is the connection between the active master in the primary region and the passive master in the secondary region secured?
options: A) Using an Amazon cross-region link that is TLS 1.2 encrypted[cite: 10]
B) Using an unencrypted AWS Direct Connect Gateway
C) Using a CloudFront Edge Cache SSL tunnel
D) Using MACsec hardware-level encryption exclusively
exp: The ElastiCache diagram explicitly points to the inter-region connection as an 'Amazon cross-region link (TLS 1.2 encrypted)'[cite: 10].

q: When scaling Amazon DocumentDB for read performance across AZ1, AZ2, and AZ3, how does the Primary instance interact with the distributed storage volume?
options: A) The Primary instance performs both Reads and Writes against the shared Distributed storage volume[cite: 10]
B) The Primary instance only writes data to AZ1, which is then asynchronously copied to Replica instances
C) The Primary instance performs Reads only, while Replicas handle all Write traffic
D) The Distributed storage volume is segmented so the Primary instance can only communicate with AZ1 and AZ2
exp: The DocumentDB architectural diagram shows the 'Instance (Primary)' performing both 'Reads' and 'Writes' against the unified 'Distributed storage volume' that spans AZ1, AZ2, and AZ3[cite: 10].

q: In a highly performant Amazon OpenSearch cluster utilizing a steady state across three zones, how is data replicated between the Active primary nodes in Zone-A and Zone-B?
options: A) Synchronous Replication[cite: 10]
B) It occurs over the Search Endpoint
C) Asynchronous Replication
D) Using a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) buffer
exp: The OpenSearch diagram depicts 'Synchronous Replication' between the Active nodes in Zone-A and Zone-B, both sitting behind the shared 'Search Endpoint'[cite: 10].

q: How does DynamoDB Accelerated Cache (DAX) offload read performance for an application?
options: A) The application integrates a DAX Client, which communicates with a clustered in-memory CACHE before falling back to the Amazon DynamoDB table[cite: 10]
B) The application uses Amazon CloudFront to cache DynamoDB JSON responses at edge locations
C) DAX forces the DynamoDB table to convert to a relational schema for faster indexed lookups
D) DAX spins up EC2 read replicas across multiple VPCs
exp: The DAX architecture diagram illustrates the application utilizing a 'Dax Client' inside an EC2 instance that queries the 'DAX Cluster' (CACHE) before reaching Amazon DynamoDB[cite: 10].

q: When a client makes a request to Amazon CloudFront that requires executing edge compute logic to manipulate the request BEFORE checking the local edge cache, which service handles this request?
options: A) CloudFront Functions (Viewer Request)[cite: 10]
B) Lambda@Edge Functions (Origin Request)
C) API Gateway Cache
D) NGINX Proxy
exp: The CloudFront caching diagram shows 'CloudFront Functions' acting on the 'Viewer Request' before the traffic hits the 'CloudFront Edge Cache'[cite: 10].

q: According to the advanced CloudFront caching architecture, at what point in the request flow does Lambda@Edge execute an 'Origin Request' function?
options: A) After passing through the CloudFront Edge Cache but before hitting the CloudFront Regional Edge Cache[cite: 10]
B) Before reaching the CloudFront Edge Cache, directly interacting with the Client
C) After the Origin returns a response to the CloudFront Regional Edge Cache
D) Inside the Amazon VPC hosting the origin server
exp: The diagram maps the flow: Client -> CloudFront Edge Cache -> (Lambda@Edge Origin Request) -> CloudFront Regional Edge Cache -> Origin[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO targets can Amazon API Gateway serve cached and uncached responses from, according to the performance offloading architecture? (Select 2)
options: A) Lambda Functions[cite: 10]
B) Public Endpoints on Amazon EC2[cite: 10]
C) On-premises tape drives via Storage Gateway
D) DynamoDB DAX cache clusters directly
exp: The API Gateway offloading diagram shows API Gateway routing traffic to Lambda Functions, Public Endpoints on Amazon EC2, Any other AWS service, and All publicly accessible endpoints[cite: 10].

q: Why does AWS explicitly recommend choosing serverless architectures whenever possible to improve performance?
options: A) Because serverless typically scales better as it provisions capacity automatically on a per-request basis[cite: 10]
B) Because serverless databases use synchronous multi-region master nodes that eliminate read latency entirely
C) Because serverless eliminates all data egress charges
D) Because serverless instances do not utilize underlying host hypervisors
exp: The 'Servered vs Serverless' slide states: 'AWS wants you to choose serverless whenever possible, and it usually scales better since it is on a per-request basis'[cite: 10].

q: In the servered versus serverless architecture diagram for Amazon Aurora, which TWO instance roles are depicted spanning across Availability Zones? (Select 2)
options: A) Writer[cite: 10]
B) Reader[cite: 10]
C) Redshift Coordinator
D) Redis Cache Master
exp: The diagram displays a compute layer with a 'Writer' in AZ1, and a 'Reader' in both AZ2 and AZ3, all attached to the underlying Storage layer[cite: 10].

q: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework for performance, what is the primary benefit of implementing a deployment pipeline (CI/CD) for infrastructure?
options: A) It allows deploying infrastructure in a repeatable, consistent, and low-cost fashion as the team iterates rapidly[cite: 10]
B) It automatically writes IAM policies using natural language processing
C) It encrypts network traffic using MACsec at Layer 2
D) It eliminates the need for manual code reviews
exp: The text states that using a CI/CD pipeline for infrastructure 'allows you to deploy in a repeatable, consistent, and low-cost fashion as you iterate'[cite: 10].

q: When automating performance tests as part of a deployment process, which approach does the framework suggest for executing long-running benchmarks without stalling the primary deployment pipeline?
options: A) Make the performance test part of the pipeline asynchronous from the rest of the build, or run tests overnight using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances[cite: 10]
B) Force the pipeline to wait synchronously until all 24-hour performance tests conclude
C) Skip performance testing entirely if unit tests pass
D) Run the tests exclusively in the production environment during peak hours
exp: For long-running tests, the framework suggests making them asynchronous from the rest of the build or running them overnight using cost-effective EC2 Spot Instances[cite: 10].

q: According to Architecture Selection best practice PERF01-BP06, what is the recommended method to finalize an architectural decision when multiple valid cloud resources exist?
options: A) Use benchmarking to drive architectural decisions[cite: 10]
B) Always select the cheapest resource type regardless of performance
C) Use manual provisioning without CloudFormation
D) Rely strictly on default AWS quota limits
exp: PERF01-BP06 specifically advises to 'Use benchmarking to drive architectural decisions' to ensure the chosen resource meets the data-driven performance criteria[cite: 10].

q: Which action must an architect take to ensure they can adequately right-size compute resources over time? (Referencing PERF02-BP03)
options: A) Collect compute-related metrics[cite: 10]
B) Disconnect EC2 instances from the internet
C) Prevent autoscaling groups from shrinking
D) Implement static IAM permissions boundaries
exp: PERF02-BP03 dictates that architects must 'Collect compute-related metrics' to evaluate how the workload behaves and properly configure and right-size resources[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO techniques are recommended by the AWS Well-Architected Framework to improve Performance Visibility during investigations? (Select 2)
options: A) Overlaying performance metrics over architecture diagrams[cite: 10]
B) Overlaying performance metrics over call graphs or code to identify issues quickly[cite: 10]
C) Printing raw CloudWatch log streams into unformatted text files
D) Manually calculating daily averages without visualizing outlier percentiles
exp: The framework suggests using visualization techniques 'that make it clear where performance issues... occur. Overlay performance metrics over architecture diagrams, call graphs, or code can help identify issues quickly'[cite: 10].

q: When evaluating the optimal data management solution, which of the following is NOT listed in the framework as a core access or storage characteristic to consider?
options: A) The exact physical location of the AWS data center rack[cite: 10]
B) Access patterns (random or sequential)[cite: 10]
C) Frequency of access (online, offline, archival)[cite: 10]
D) Frequency of update (WORM, dynamic)[cite: 10]
exp: The optimal data management solution varies based on data type, access patterns (random/sequential), required throughput, frequency of access (online/offline), frequency of update (WORM/dynamic), and durability constraints. Physical rack location is not a customer-managed selection criteria[cite: 10].

q: According to Networking Performance best practice PERF04-BP05, what should be evaluated to maximize the performance of data in transit?
options: A) Choose network protocols to improve performance[cite: 10]
B) Ensure all internal VPC communication routes through an external Internet Gateway
C) Limit all data transfer strictly to 100 Mbps
D) Only utilize IPv4, ignoring IPv6 capabilities
exp: PERF04-BP05 states to 'Choose network protocols to improve performance', which involves selecting the right transport (e.g., TCP vs UDP, or newer protocols like HTTP/2 or HTTP/3) depending on the workload's latency and throughput needs[cite: 10].

q: In the autoscaling architectural diagram, how does the Application Load Balancer distribute traffic to instances spawned by the Auto Scaling group?
options: A) Across instances residing in multiple subnets spanning different Availability Zones[cite: 10]
B) Only to instances in the single public subnet of the first Availability Zone
C) By bypassing the EC2 security group entirely
D) By forcing the traffic through an external NAT Gateway first
exp: The diagram displays an Application Load Balancer distributing HTTP/S requests across an Auto Scaling group containing instances in Subnets across multiple Availability Zones[cite: 10].

q: What does the AWS Well-Architected Framework identify as the usual root cause for architectures performing poorly over time?
options: A) A non-existent or broken performance review process[cite: 10]
B) The failure of AWS physical hardware
C) Using serverless compute options instead of EC2
D) Excessive use of CloudFront edge caching
exp: The text states: 'Architectures performing poorly is usually the result of a non-existent or broken performance review process. If your architecture is performing poorly, implementing a performance review process allows you to drive iterative improvement'[cite: 10].

q: How does defining Infrastructure as Code (IaC) directly contribute to performance efficiency according to the Process and Culture guidelines?
options: A) It allows infrastructure to be placed into source control alongside application code, applying standard software development practices to iterate rapidly[cite: 10]
B) It encrypts physical hard drives automatically
C) It replaces all manual database schema migrations
D) It increases the clock speed of underlying CPU processors
exp: IaC (like CloudFormation) allows you to 'place your infrastructure into source control alongside your application code... so you can iterate rapidly', a key driver for continual performance optimization[cite: 10].

q: In the complex load distribution diagram involving multiple brands, what architectural components are placed between the public internet requests and the final Application Load Balancers? (Select 2)
options: A) NGINX Proxy servers[cite: 10]
B) Initial Elastic Load Balancing layer[cite: 10]
C) Direct Connect Gateways
D) Amazon ElastiCache Clusters
exp: The diagram displays www.example.com hitting an 'Elastic Load Balancing' instance, routing to multiple 'NGINX PROXY' servers, which then route to further 'Elastic Load Balancing' instances for the respective brands[cite: 10].

q: To maximize performance and cache hit rates, CloudFront utilizes a two-tier caching architecture. According to the provided diagram, what sits between the CloudFront Edge Cache and the Origin?
options: A) CloudFront Regional Edge Cache[cite: 10]
B) CloudFront Functions
C) DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
D) Route 53 DNS Resolver
exp: The architectural flow shows the 'CloudFront Edge Cache' backed by the 'CloudFront Regional Edge Cache' before requests finally hit the Origin[cite: 10].

q: When setting up Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), what is an example of a business metric that can indicate performance-related financial efficiency?
options: A) The aggregate cumulative cost per request[cite: 10]
B) The garbage collection rate of the JVM[cite: 10]
C) The count of active worker threads[cite: 10]
D) The time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for web page rendering[cite: 10]
exp: While thread count, TTFB, and garbage collection are technical metrics, 'aggregate cumulative cost per request' is explicitly defined as a business metric that can alert you to ways to drive down costs while maintaining performance[cite: 10].

q: What does the AWS Well-Architected Framework suggest as a mechanism to offset physical network constraints, such as the fixed location of users or on-premises resources?
options: A) Utilizing edge locations or strategic resource placement[cite: 10]
B) Upgrading desktop computer RAM on user laptops
C) Disabling IPv6 routing entirely
D) Refactoring code from Java to C++
exp: The text states that physical constraints 'can be offset with edge locations or resource placement' to improve latency and throughput despite geographic distance[cite: 10].

q: According to the Autoscaling vs Manual Scaling matrix, which TWO configuration methods are supported for configuring autoscaling on Amazon EMR? (Select 2)
options: A) Console access[cite: 10]
B) CLI access[cite: 10]
C) Physical dip-switches
D) Root kernel manipulation
exp: The matrix indicates that Amazon EMR supports autoscaling configuration via Console, CLI, SDK, and CloudFormation (all marked 'Yes')[cite: 10].

q: In an offloading strategy, how does the Amazon DocumentDB architecture diagram conceptually parallel an Amazon RDS/Aurora setup?
options: A) It utilizes a primary instance for writes and read replicas to offload read traffic, all connected to a shared distributed storage volume[cite: 10]
B) It utilizes synchronous multi-master write replication across all AZs
C) It forces all replicas to handle write traffic exclusively
D) It relies on an external Redis cache to store all documents
exp: The DocumentDB diagram mirrors Aurora's read-scaling architecture, showing a Primary instance handling writes/reads, and Replica instances offloading reads, backed by a 'Distributed storage volume'[cite: 10].

q: A company is using Amazon S3 to store relational data but finds performance unacceptably slow for complex queries. The architect suggests switching to Amazon RDS. Which performance principle drives this specific design change?
options: A) Consider Mechanical Sympathy[cite: 10]
B) Use Serverless Architectures[cite: 10]
C) Go Global in Minutes[cite: 10]
D) Democratize Advanced Technologies[cite: 10]
exp: The 'Applying Performance Design Principles' slide explicitly maps 'S3 is not performing well as a database' -> 'Consider Mechanical Sympathy' -> 'Consider switching to RDS or another database technology'[cite: 10].

q: To ensure load generation scripts effectively test application performance at scale without incurring massive fixed costs, what specific compute strategy does AWS recommend for executing these load tests?
options: A) Using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to generate the load cost-effectively[cite: 10]
B) Using dedicated bare-metal servers hosted on-premises
C) Using manual clicking by QA testers
D) Running the tests exclusively on the AWS Management Console backend
exp: The framework explicitly states: 'Consider using AWS Marketplace solutions and Spot Instances - they can be cost-effective ways to generate the load'[cite: 10].

q: Which TWO benefits are directly attributed to the 'Go global in minutes' performance design principle?
options: A) Providing lower latency to customers by deploying workloads in multiple AWS Regions[cite: 10]
B) Delivering a better customer experience at minimal cost[cite: 10]
C) Mandating that all data must reside in a single geographical data center
D) Increasing the complexity of manual deployments
exp: The text states: 'Deploying your workload in multiple AWS Regions around the world allows you to provide lower latency and a better experience for your customers at minimal cost'[cite: 10].

q: During a performance review, an architect notices that an API is frequently fetching the exact same static dataset from a backend database, causing latency. According to the general concepts of offloading and load distribution, what is the most performant way to resolve this?
options: A) Implement an API Gateway Cache or a caching layer like ElastiCache to offload the database and serve rapid responses[cite: 10]
B) Increase the size of the database server's EBS volume
C) Force the API to query the database using unencrypted HTTP
D) Move the database to a completely different AWS Region
exp: The Offloading and Load Distribution modules emphasize that caching goes beyond databases, specifically highlighting the use of 'API Gateway Cache' or 'ElastiCache' to intercept requests and improve performance by offloading the backend[cite: 10].
